prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of proposals (ideological framing removed)

Core aims
- Freeze most non-essential immigration; end Channel small-boat crossings via detention, offshore processing, rapid returns, and legal changes.
- Eliminate NHS waiting lists while keeping care free at point of use.
- Raise the income tax threshold to £20,000; cut household energy costs by scrapping green levies and expanding domestic oil and gas.

Immigration
- Freeze non-essential visas; exception for essential skills (mainly health/care).
- Create a new immigration department; leave certain international legal frameworks to enable removals.
- Detain and rapidly process illegal arrivals (offshore if needed); bar asylum claims from safe-country entrants; no legal aid for non-citizens.
- Immediate deportation of foreign offenders after sentences; potential citizenship removal for serious crimes.
- Restrict student dependants; close abuse of study routes.
- Five-year residency and employment before accessing benefits.
- Employer immigration tax: raise NI to 20% for foreign workers (exempt health/care and very small firms).
- Claimed savings: £5–10bn pa; employer tax yield: £4bn pa.

Public spending and waste
- Stop paying interest on QE reserves to commercial banks (claimed saving ~£35bn pa).
- 5% efficiency saving across departments (~£50bn pa).
- Halve foreign aid (~£6bn); strengthen HMRC to reduce the tax gap; cut retained EU-era regulation.
- Total “waste” savings potential stated: ~£91bn pa.

Tax and economy (personal)
- Lift income tax start point to £20,000; higher rate from £70,000.
- Cut fuel duty by 20p/litre; scrap VAT on energy and environmental levies.
- Reduce residential stamp duty (0% to £750k; 2% £750k–£1.5m; 4% above).
- Restore VAT-free tourist shopping; raise IHT threshold to £2m with 20% rate above.
- Cost estimate: £70bn pa.

Business and growth
- No corporation tax for profits under £100k; main rate to 20%, then 15% in year 3.
- Abolish IR35; raise VAT threshold to £150k.
- Abolish business rates for high-street SMEs, offset by a 4% online delivery tax on large multinationals.
- Planning reform; deregulation to ease hiring/firing; major tax simplification.
- Cost estimate: £18bn pa.

NHS and social care
- Zero basic-rate income tax for NHS/social care staff for 3 years; end training caps; student loan write-off tied to service.
- Expand use of independent capacity (UK/overseas); 20% tax relief on private healthcare/insurance.
- Voucher for private treatment if GP/consultant/operation waits exceed 3/3/9 weeks.
- Efficiency measures: weekend theatres, better procurement, DNAs charged.
- Royal Commission on social care; tackle offshore tax avoidance by large care providers.
- Cost estimate: £17bn pa.

Energy and net zero
- Scrap net zero targets and related subsidies; end £10bn pa renewables subsidies via equivalent taxes.
- Fast-track North Sea oil/gas and shale pilots; expand SMRs and other technologies.
- Claimed savings: ~£30bn pa.

Law, order, and justice
- Recruit 40,000 officers over 5 years; “zero tolerance” approach; increase stop and search; mandatory prison for knife possession; life for drug trafficking.
- New leadership standards; reduce non-operational roles; phase out PCSOs.
- Justice: automatic life for violent repeat offenders; raise budget from £10bn to £12bn; reopen magistrates’ courts; build 10,000 detention places; revise hate crime definitions.
- Costs: policing £3bn pa; justice £2bn pa.

Education and families
- Curriculum changes; restrictions on gender-related measures in schools; single-sex facilities.
- 20% tax relief on independent school fees; scrap interest on student loans; limit undergraduate numbers; raise entry standards.
- Expand PRUs; promote 2-year degrees.
- Family measures: transferable marriage allowance (as finances allow); front-load child benefit ages 1–4; smartphone/online safety reviews.
- Cost: education £5bn pa; families £8bn pa.

Housing
- Fast-track brownfield development; prioritise locals in social housing; restore mortgage interest deductibility for landlords; drop Renters’ Reform Bill; strengthen leaseholder protections. Cost neutral.

Transport and infrastructure
- Scrap remaining HS2 (one-off £25bn saving); ban ULEZ/CAZ/LTNs; no ICE bans.
- Regional road/rail upgrades.
- New utility ownership model: 50% public, 50% UK pension funds; cap standing charges.
- Savings: £25bn one-off; £5bn pa.

Agriculture and fishing
- Farming budget to £3bn; replace climate-linked subsidies with direct payments; reduce red tape; targets to raise domestic sourcing, especially in public sector.
- Fishing: end automatic foreign access; paid licences; expand enforcement; ban supertrawlers and pulse fishing; rebuild processing; support fleet.
- Costs: agriculture £2bn pa; fishing £2bn pa.

Constitution and governance
- Human rights framework changes; reform second chamber and civil service leadership; restrict postal voting; consider PR via referendum; British Bill of Rights.
- “Reclaiming” measures: free speech bill, replace equalities law, reform BBC funding, new anti-corruption unit, oppose CBDC/cashless, review WHO arrangements.

Funding summary (as stated)
- Estimated annual savings and extra growth: ~£160bn pa.
- Estimated annual costs: ~£141bn pa.
